intervention_label: Confirm DLL3 by IHC (SP347) on tumor — diagnostic gate
expected_benefit: Resolves whether the DLL3-directed pathway is open. Trial NCT06788938 enforces ≥25% (stage 1) or ≥1% (stage 2) by IHC.
key_risks: if negative, the DLL3-directed pathway is foreclosed
preference_alignment: Aligns with all stated preferences — non-toxic, gates the user-preferred trial option.
guideline_status: Implicit in every modern targeted-therapy guideline; specifically required by NCT06788938.
rationale_summary: All five personas converged on DLL3 IHC as the precondition. RNA expression alone does not establish membrane DLL3, and IHC is the standard gating biomarker for every DLL3-directed therapy in current clinical use.
open_questions: Will the SP347 antibody assay be available at the treating institution?
Is sufficient archival or fresh tumor available?
likelihood_of_effect: Diagnostic certainty — resolves whether the DLL3-directed pathway is reachable; required by NCT06788938 (≥25% stage 1, ≥1% stage 2).
toxicity_burden: Low (none — diagnostic test on archival tissue)
overall: Non-toxic precondition that gates rank 2 entirely; run regardless of which therapy is ultimately chosen.

expected_benefit: If mechanism translates from SCLC: median OS 13.6 vs 8.3 mo (HR 0.60) in DeLLphi-304 SCLC; ORR ~40% in DeLLphi-301. Cross-tumor extrapolation to osteosarcoma is unproven — the trial design exists precisely to test this.
key_risks: no prior osteosarcoma data — cross-tumor translation is the open question
preference_alignment: Strong match: high-risk-high-reward + prefers_trials. Conditional on positive DLL3 IHC.
guideline_status: Off-guideline for osteosarcoma; trial enrollment is NCCN cat-1 for relapsed disease.
rationale_summary: Conditional on positive DLL3 IHC. Conservative's earlier toxicity veto was contingent on biomarker confirmation and lifts here. Concensusite endorses on guideline-aligned trial-enrollment principle. The critic's evidence-quality dissent persists (no published osteosarcoma data with tarlatamab; cross-tumor translation unproven). Two endorsements from round 1 (risktaker, advocate) plus the post-IHC veto-lift from conservative and qualified-now-endorse from concensusite yield a positive agreement score. Foreclosed if IHC negative.
open_questions: Slot availability at NCT06788938 enrolling sites
Cross-tumor translatability of DLL3 BiTE mechanism — first osteosarcoma cohort
likelihood_of_effect: Cross-tumor extrapolation: SCLC OS HR 0.60 (DeLLphi-304); ORR ~40% (DeLLphi-301). Osteosarcoma efficacy is the open question NCT06788938 will answer.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (CRS ~50% mostly G1-2; CRS G≥3 ~1%; ICANS-like ~10%; inpatient cycle-1 step-up dosing required)

counter_productive_moa.description: On-mechanism CNS bystander T-cell activation drives ICANS; possible DLL3 antigen-loss escape on repeated dosing

overall: The only DLL3-directed option when IHC is positive — preference-aligned but cross-tumor translation untested; foreclosed if IHC negative.

expected_benefit: mPFS 3.6 vs 1.7 mo (SARC024, HR 0.42); replicated in REGOBONE (mPFS 16.4 vs 4.1 wk, non-progression at 8 wk 65%).
preference_alignment: Aligns with case (relapsed metastatic osteosarcoma); oral; no IV chair time. Independent of DLL3 IHC result.
rationale_summary: Strongest replicated 2L+ osteosarcoma RCT evidence base — two independent placebo-controlled trials (SARC024 + REGOBONE) converge on PFS benefit. All five personas endorsed; no dissent. Biomarker-independent backbone regardless of IHC outcome.
open_questions: Which dose-reduction protocol best balances efficacy preservation against hand-foot toxicity
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate. mPFS 3.6 vs 1.7 mo (SARC024, HR 0.42, p=0.017); independently replicated in REGOBONE — strongest 2L+ osteosarcoma RCT evidence base.
toxicity_burden: High (G3+ AEs 70-76%: hand-foot, hypertension, fatigue, mucositis; ~65% require dose reduction; no treatment-related deaths)

counter_productive_moa.description: Anti-angiogenic mechanism can impair wound healing and raise bleeding risk; no on-target counter-productive vector

overall: Strongest replicated 2L+ osteosarcoma RCT evidence; biomarker-independent backbone regardless of IHC.

expected_benefit: ORR 11.9% (CABONE osteosarcoma cohort, n=42); mPFS 6.2 mo; 6-mo non-progression 33.3%.
preference_alignment: Aligns with case; oral; biomarker-independent. Lower agreement_score gap behind regorafenib reflects single-arm design.
guideline_status: NCCN cat-2B; supports the active AOST2032 frontline phase-2/3 trial.
rationale_summary: Pre-specified osteosarcoma cohort within CABONE (single-arm phase-2). All five personas endorsed; no dissent. Reasonable 2L+ option in non-trial setting; ranks below regorafenib because single-arm vs two replicating placebo-controlled RCTs, not because of any board-level objection.
open_questions: Sequence after regorafenib failure — minimal head-to-head data
likelihood_of_effect: Modest. ORR ~12% in CABONE osteosarcoma cohort (n=42); mPFS 6.2 mo. Single-arm phase-2 evidence — supportive but not RCT-grade.
toxicity_burden: High (G3+ AEs ~68%: hypertension, hand-foot, hypophosphatemia, transaminitis; thromboembolism ~7%)

counter_productive_moa.description: VEGFR-driven thromboembolism / wound-healing impairment is class-effect off-target; no on-mechanism counter-productive vector

overall: Single-arm sarcoma-cohort signal; biomarker-independent fallback when an RCT-grade option is exhausted or unavailable.
